calls.title: GrowthBook Commercial Discussion
calls.summary: The discussions revolved around a straightforward commercial model with a fixed annual subscription for an experimentation platform, starting at $75,000 for 60 experiments. Pricing stability is ensured by charging based on experiments rather than traffic or users. Client targets were highlighted, with a goal of 312 annual experiments, though a more achievable target is 120. Urgent migration from the current platform, Unleash, is ongoing, with an estimated implementation timeline of four to six weeks. The decision-making process involves multiple teams, including product and engineering, with a focus on platform suitability and IT security. Growth Book's support and onboarding model was underscored, aimed at facilitating a smooth transition, with surveys being deployed to capture preferences ahead of a final decision expected next week.
calls.keywords: Experimentation, Pricing Model, Feature Flags, Migration, Deployment Timeline, Decision Process

calls.summary:
# GrowthBook Commercial Discussion
Date: 2026-09-15 | Duration: 30.68000030517578m

## Summary
María and James discussed whether Growth Book could replace AB Tasty while es.guess faces strict post-acquisition financial scrutiny. AB Tasty auto-renewed in August for one year at €40,800 annually, covering unlimited tests and personalization, so María must consult legal and AB Tasty about exit or amendment options. Growth Book proposed experiment-based pricing starting at €95,000 annually, including unlimited traffic and feature flags, but the increase is difficult to justify without clear ROI or added value. James highlighted BigQuery integration, improved dashboards, a visual no-code editor, Figma integration, AI-driven experiment suggestions, and hierarchical component control. María said these capabilities could improve data trust and simplify testing, while emphasizing that finance requires one supplier and strong cost justification. James offered six months of free usage, potential discounts, flexible contract terms, and a possible case study collaboration. María will review the proposal with finance, legal, and AB Tasty, while James will send revised pricing by email; a product demo and further discussions remain possible.

## Keywords
A/B testing, contract renewal, pricing negotiation, feature flags, no-code visual editor, budgeting constraints

## Action Items

**María Fernández**
Discuss current AB Tasty contract terms with legal and finance to explore early termination or amendments (08:54)
Review pricing and commercial proposal internally and with AB Tasty, then follow up with James via email with decision or negotiation points (26:19)
Confirm willingness to engage in case study or joint best practice sharing with GrowthBook after internal discussions (27:50)

**James Shannon**
Send revised commercial proposals reflecting six months free usage offer and potential pricing adjustments for contract signing by end October (25:25)
Follow up with María by email with commercial options and possible solutions to accommodate budget constraints (29:27)
Provide a demo or additional information on GrowthBook’s no-code visual experimentation editor if requested by María’s team (15:00)
